# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Packet Capture

**Evidence:** `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 packets, 27 MB, capture window 2026-01-28 03:04:03 – 03:14:27 UTC+4, ~10.5 min). No IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; all findings below are derived directly from the pcap via `tshark`.

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.1.21.58 | DHCP, all traffic |
| MAC | 00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2 | Ethernet frames |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-ES9F3ML | DHCP Option 12, NBNS registration |
| Domain/workgroup | WIN11OFFICE / WIN11OFFICE.COM | NBNS, Kerberos realm |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString between 10.1.21.58 and DC 10.1.21.2 |

Host is a domain-joined Windows 11 workstation (Chrome 144 / Edge 144 UA strings, WebGL renderer strings show AMD Radeon R9 200-series GPU under ANGLE, 12 logical cores).

## Malware family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS ruleset/alerts were provided with this evidence, so no signature hits exist to cite). Traffic behavior is consistent with a **fingerprinting/tracking gate (TDS) used ahead of a commodity info-stealer payload delivery**, matching the pattern commonly associated with **Lumma Stealer** distribution chains (fake file-host lure → archive download → browser-fingerprint C2 check-in using `id=`/`token=`/`act=` parameters). Confidence is moderate-behavioral: the C2 URI grammar and fingerprinting payload are a strong match to that family's known panel style, but no file hash or static signature was recoverable to confirm it definitively.

## Attack chain (chronological, all times 2026-01-28, UTC+4)

1. **03:04:49** — DNS lookup for `hiyter.com` → 104.21.22.231 (Cloudflare-fronted). Likely initial lure/landing page.
2. **03:04:49** — DNS lookup for `media.megafilehub4.lat` → 104.21.48.156. Fake file-hosting clone domain.
3. **03:04:52** — DNS lookup for `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` → 104.21.46.67. TLS session to this host (10.1.21.58:54840 ↔ 104.21.46.67:443) transferred **~16 MB** over 22 seconds — consistent in size/shape with an archive/installer payload download. Content is TLS-encrypted; no plaintext file name or hash could be recovered.
4. **03:05:34** — DNS lookup for `whooptm.cyou` → 62.72.32.156. Short TLS session (~12 KB).
5. **03:05:36 – 03:06:06** — Sustained beaconing to **`whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49)**, both plaintext HTTP (port 80) and TLS (port 443), across many short-lived TCP connections roughly 1–3 seconds apart. Confirmed via `tshark` HTTP object export:
   - `GET /api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
   - `POST /api/set_agent?...&agent=Chrome&act=log` (repeated with `agent=Edge`)
   - The GET returns a JavaScript fingerprinting payload that harvests: navigator properties, WebGL vendor/renderer/canvas fingerprint (base64 PNG), screen geometry, hardware concurrency, installed fonts, audio-context capabilities, plugin list, and a WebRTC ICE candidate/SDP for local-IP leak.
   - The POST `act=log` request exfiltrates that full fingerprint JSON back to the same host/token, for both a "Chrome" and an "Edge" identity — i.e., the malware polled/re-registered itself under two different browser-agent labels against the same victim `id`/`token`.
6. **03:06:06** — DNS lookup for `holiday-forever.cc` → 80.97.160.24, followed by a TLS session downloading ~119 KB to the victim.
7. **03:06:10** — DNS lookup for `communicationfirewall-security.cc` → 104.21.9.36 (Cloudflare-fronted), TLS session downloading ~107 KB to the victim across two connections.

No further contact with any of these domains occurs after 03:06:11; the remainder of the capture (03:06 – 03:14) is routine Windows/Microsoft/Google background traffic (telemetry, MSN, Office, Google services) plus normal AD traffic (Kerberos, LDAP/CLDAP, SMB2/DCERPC to DC 10.1.21.2) — no indication of AD lateral movement or credential-dumping activity; the elevated SMB2/DCERPC/LSARPC/SAMR volume is consistent with routine domain-workstation chatter with the DC, not attacker tooling.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / malicious endpoints (IP:port):**
- 104.21.22.231:443, 172.67.207.145 — `hiyter.com`
- 104.21.48.156:443, 172.67.154.67 — `media.megafilehub4.lat`
- 104.21.46.67:443, 172.67.136.13 — `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (payload-delivery-sized transfer, ~16 MB)
- 62.72.32.156:443 — `whooptm.cyou`
- **153.92.1.49:80 and :443 — `whitepepper.su`** (primary fingerprinting/check-in C2)
- 80.97.160.24:443 — `holiday-forever.cc`
- 104.21.9.36:443, 172.67.141.109 — `communicationfirewall-security.cc`

**Malicious domains:**
- hiyter.com
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- whooptm.cyou
- whitepepper.su
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc

**Malicious URLs (observed, plaintext):**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

**Victim/campaign identifier:** `id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`, `token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b` (used consistently across the whitepepper.su session).

**Transferred files / hashes:** No file with a recoverable name or computable SHA256 was observed in cleartext. The likely payload transfer to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67:443, ~16 MB) and the secondary downloads from `holiday-forever.cc` (~119 KB) and `communicationfirewall-security.cc` (~107 KB) were carried entirely inside TLS and cannot be extracted or hashed without the session keys, which are not present in this evidence set.
